subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work/PB400.md - REPAIRED. The rule is a claim about what a condition-name YIELDS after SET ... TO ON/OFF, and the SET/read-side state was already shared and correct; what held the row open was a legal context in which the condition-name could not be WRITTEN at all. `EVALUATE W-ON WHEN TRUE` over a SPECIAL-NAMES switch was refused with two COBOL1634s naming the subject 'an identifier', while the level-88 spelling in the identical position compiled and ran and the same switch name worked as an EVALUATE OBJECT, in IF and in PERFORM UNTIL - the asymmetry that proved it a classifier hole rather than a Table-15 fact. Cause: EvaluateBinder had TWO per-side classifiers, and only the object one asked ConditionBinder.BareOperandAsCondition, the single helper that recognises a switch-status condition-name (8.8.4.6). They are now ONE (EvaluateBinder.BareOperandKind over ConditionBinder.AnalyzeBareOperand, mapped across Table 15's axes by EvaluateOperandCombinations.AsSubjectOperand), so a condition form added to one side is recognised on the other by construction, and EvaluateOperandClassifierDriftTests measures that symmetry over every bare-operand condition shape in both positions and both polarities. The golden observes the promised truth value through the subject position at --std 85 for ON and for OFF, alongside the object position and the level-88 control.
